gen-gf-shippori-mincho-b1-fs-bespoke-san: Bespoke Sans reads sharp and refined, its curves leaving generous gaps before they reach the stem, while Shippori Mincho B1 above it swells only slightly in its bowls. Give the sans a little more size.
gen-gf-signika-fs-literata: Approachable Signika keeps its letters plain and low in contrast, nothing fussy. Literata takes over underneath with sturdy thin lines, slightly heavier thick ones and a bookish, mellow serif voice.
gen-gf-signika-negative-fs-literata: Crisp and uncluttered, Signika Negative has plain, low-contrast letters that get straight to the point. And Literata settles in beneath with open-mouthed curves and moderate modulation, so extended reading feels bookish and unhurried.
gen-gf-sirin-stencil-bitter: Bitter reads dependable and grounded, with a very large lowercase eye and an s you can see straight through. Sirin Stencil overhead is the loud one.
gen-gf-sirin-stencil-instrument-sans: Clean and modern, Instrument Sans has c shapes whose ends point apart like open pincers and a barely there step up to capitals. But Sirin Stencil, with its bead-sized counters, is the one to keep bigger.
gen-gf-sirin-stencil-inter: Drilled-glass counters, bold and unvarying. Inter follows with a smooth, tube-like look and tall lowercase, so Sirin Stencil does the shouting while Inter does the explaining.
gen-gf-sirin-stencil-mulish: Bold stencil letters with counters like drilled glass beads, then a soft landing. Mulish drops all thick-and-thin modulation and opens its apertures like a horseshoe magnet, and that smooth modern friendliness is the whole point.
gen-gf-sirin-stencil-poppins: Poppins brings rope-loose curves and a tall, sturdy lowercase with no thick-thin flicker to distract. And Sirin Stencil, commanding and bold, gives the page its punch from above.
gen-gf-sixtyfour-fs-bespoke-sans: Sixtyfour sets typewriter-like letters with terminals tucked tight, leaving gaps like wide stitches in coarse thread, so it feels precise and structured. Bespoke Sans opens everything back up.
gen-gf-slackey-bitter: Slackey is loud and expressive, with gentle swelling on its curves. Bitter underneath is the steadier half, with a very large lowercase eye and a visible gap in each s, and that grounded slab-serif calm is the pair's strongest card.
